1| """Token-chain: DeepSeek writes a tiny work order; local Ollama executes it.
2| 
3| Purpose
4| -------
5| Prove Grok (or operator) can *direct* DeepSeek as a planner seat that emits a
6| frozen local_work_order.v1, then a dumb local seat executes without burning
7| frontier tokens on tool thrash.
8| 
9| Dashboard: POST /api/v1/token-chain
10| CLI:       python main.py token-chain [--goal ...] [--dry] [--live]
11| """
12| from __future__ import annotations
13| 
14| import json
15| import re
16| import time
17| from datetime import datetime, timezone
18| from pathlib import Path
19| from typing import Any
20| 
21| from config import ROOT
22| 
23| 
24| def _rel_posix(path) -> str:
25|     """Repo-relative posix path, absolute when outside ROOT.
26| 
27|     Cause (ball3 follow-up sweep 2026-09-29): display/receipt derivations
28|     raised ValueError whenever the path lived outside the repo (the suite
29|     runs use an out-of-repo pytest basetemp). Same fix as the driver-meter
30|     lane's _rel_posix in tools/stealth_driver.py.
31|     """
32|     try:
33|         return Path(path).relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
34|     except ValueError:
35|         return Path(path).as_posix()
36| 
37| 
38| 
39| SCHEMA = "local_work_order.v1"
40| RUN_DIR = ROOT / "memory" / "runs" / "token_chain"
41| ALLOWED_OPS = frozenset({"read_file", "list_dir", "count_lines", "write_run_note"})
42| MAX_STEPS = 5
43| 
44| 
45| def _now() -> str:
46|     return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
47| 
48| 
49| def _ensure() -> None:
50|     RUN_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
51| 
52| 
53| def _safe_under_root(rel: str) -> Path:
54|     """Resolve path under ROOT; reject escapes and secret files."""
55|     raw = (rel or "").strip().replace("\\", "/")
56|     if not raw or raw.startswith("/") or ".." in raw.split("/"):
57|         raise ValueError(f"unsafe path: {rel!r}")
58|     low = raw.lower()
59|     for ban in (".env", "credentials", "secret", "id_rsa", "auth.json"):
60|         if ban in low:
61|             raise ValueError(f"prohibited path: {rel!r}")
62|     p = (ROOT / raw).resolve()
63|     root = ROOT.resolve()
64|     if not str(p).startswith(str(root)):
65|         raise ValueError(f"path escapes root: {rel!r}")
66|     return p
67|

69| def parse_work_order(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
70|     """Extract local_work_order.v1 JSON from model text."""
71|     s = (text or "").strip()
72|     if not s:
73|         raise ValueError("empty plan text")
74|     # fenced json
75|     m = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*?\})\s*```", s, re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
76|     if m:
77|         s = m.group(1)
78|     else:
79|         start, end = s.find("{"), s.rfind("}")
80|         if start < 0 or end <= start:
81|             raise ValueError("no JSON object in plan")
82|         s = s[start : end + 1]
83|     data = json.loads(s)
84|     if not isinstance(data, dict):
85|         raise ValueError("plan must be object")
86|     data["schema"] = SCHEMA
87|     steps = data.get("steps")
88|     if not isinstance(steps, list) or not steps:
89|         raise ValueError("steps required")
90|     if len(steps) > MAX_STEPS:
91|         data["steps"] = steps[:MAX_STEPS]
92|         data["truncated_steps"] = True
93|     clean: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
94|     for i, step in enumerate(data["steps"]):
95|         if not isinstance(step, dict):
96|             continue
97|         op = str(step.get("op") or step.get("action") or "").strip()
98|         if op not in ALLOWED_OPS:
99|             raise ValueError(f"step {i}: op {op!r} not in {sorted(ALLOWED_OPS)}")
100|         path = str(step.get("path") or "").strip()
101|         if op != "write_run_note" and not path:
102|             raise ValueError(f"step {i}: path required")
103|         if path:
104|             # validate early so bad plans never reach exec
105|             _safe_under_root(path)
106|         clean.append(
107|             {
108|                 "op": op,
109|                 "path": path,
110|                 "note": str(step.get("note") or step.get("content") or "")[:2000],
111|             }
112|         )
113|     if not clean:
114|         raise ValueError("no valid steps")
115|     data["steps"] = clean
116|     data["goal"] = str(data.get("goal") or "token-chain")[:500]
117|     data["success_criteria"] = str(data.get("success_criteria") or "all steps ok")[:500]
118|     return data
119|

121| def execute_work_order(order: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
122|     """Deterministic local executor — no LLM. Safe ops only under ROOT."""
123|     results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
124|     ok_all = True
125|     for i, step in enumerate(order.get("steps") or []):
126|         op = step["op"]
127|         t0 = time.perf_counter()
128|         try:
129|             if op == "read_file":
130|                 p = _safe_under_root(step["path"])
131|                 if not p.is_file():
132|                     raise FileNotFoundError(str(p))
133|                 text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
134|                 results.append(
135|                     {
136|                         "i": i,
137|                         "op": op,
138|                         "path": step["path"],
139|                         "ok": True,
140|                         "chars": len(text),
141|                         "preview": text[:240],
142|                         "ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
143|                     }
144|                 )
145|             elif op == "list_dir":
146|                 p = _safe_under_root(step["path"] or ".")
147|                 if not p.is_dir():
148|                     raise NotADirectoryError(str(p))
149|                 names = sorted(x.name for x in p.iterdir())[:50]
150|                 results.append(
151|                     {
152|                         "i": i,
153|                         "op": op,
154|                         "path": step["path"],
155|                         "ok": True,
156|                         "n": len(names),
157|                         "names": names,
158|                         "ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
159|                     }
160|                 )
161|             elif op == "count_lines":
162|                 p = _safe_under_root(step["path"])
163|                 n = sum(1 for _ in p.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
164|                 results.append(
165|                     {
166|                         "i": i,
167|                         "op": op,
168|                         "path": step["path"],
169|                         "ok": True,
170|                         "lines": n,
171|                         "ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
172|                     }
173|                 )
174|             elif op == "write_run_note":
175|                 _ensure()
176|                 note_path = RUN_DIR / "local_note.md"
177|                 body = (
178|                     f"# token-chain local note\n\n"
179|                     f"- ts: {_now()}\n"
180|                     f"- goal: {order.get('goal')}\n\n"
181|                     f"{step.get('note') or '(empty)'}\n"
182|                 )
183|                 note_path.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
184|                 results.append(
185|                     {
186|                         "i": i,
187|                         "op": op,
188|                         "path": "memory/runs/token_chain/local_note.md",
189|                         "ok": True,
190|                         "ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
191|                     }
192|                 )
193|             else:
194|                 raise ValueError(f"unknown op {op}")
195|         except Exception as exc:
196|             ok_all = False
197|             results.append(
198|                 {
199|                     "i": i,
200|                     "op": op,
201|                     "path": step.get("path"),
202|                     "ok": False,
203|                     "error": str(exc)[:400],
204|                     "ms": int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000),
205|                 }
206|             )
207|     return {"ok": ok_all, "results": results, "n_ok": sum(1 for r in results if r.get("ok"))}

210| def _plan_prompt(goal: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
211|     system = (
212|         "You are Mag's PLANNER seat (DeepSeek). Output ONLY one JSON object, no prose.\n"
213|         f"Schema {SCHEMA}. Allowed ops: {sorted(ALLOWED_OPS)}.\n"
214|         f"Max {MAX_STEPS} steps. Paths relative to Mag root only.\n"
215|         "Never request .env, secrets, or paths outside the repo.\n"
216|         "Prefer read_file / count_lines / list_dir on memory/improve or docs — cheap scut for local.\n"
217|         "Include write_run_note once with a 1-line summary of what local will report."
218|     )
219|     user = (
220|         f"Goal (T2 public): {goal}\n\n"
221|         "Emit JSON:\n"
222|         "{\n"
223|         f'  "schema": "{SCHEMA}",\n'
224|         '  "goal": "...",\n'
225|         '  "success_criteria": "...",\n'
226|         '  "steps": [\n'
227|         '    {"op": "read_file", "path": "memory/improve/field_brief.md"},\n'
228|         '    {"op": "count_lines", "path": "memory/improve/candidates.jsonl"},\n'
229|         '    {"op": "write_run_note", "note": "..."}\n'
230|         "  ]\n"
231|         "}\n"
232|     )
233|     return system, user

236| def _usage_tokens(resp: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, int]:
237|     u = resp.get("usage") or resp.get("meta") or {}
238|     if not isinstance(u, dict):
239|         u = {}
240|     return {
241|         "prompt_tokens": int(u.get("prompt_tokens") or u.get("input_tokens") or 0),
242|         "completion_tokens": int(u.get("completion_tokens") or u.get("output_tokens") or 0),
243|         "total_tokens": int(
244|             u.get("total_tokens")
245|             or (
246|                 int(u.get("prompt_tokens") or 0)
247|                 + int(u.get("completion_tokens") or 0)
248|             )
249|             or 0
250|         ),
251|     }
252|

254| def run_token_chain(
255|     *,
256|     goal: str | None = None,
257|     dry: bool = False,
258|     live: bool = True,
259|     planner: str = "deepseek",
260|     fixture_plan: str | None = None,
261| ) -> dict[str, Any]:
262|     """
263|     Run one chain tick.
264| 
265|     dry=True  → no model calls; use canned plan if no fixture
266|     live=True → call DeepSeek for plan, execute locally (no local LLM needed)
267|     """
268|     _ensure()
269|     goal = (goal or "Inspect improve field_brief and candidates; note top ticket ids").strip()
270|     out: dict[str, Any] = {
271|         "schema": "token_chain_run.v1",
272|         "ts": _now(),
273|         "goal": goal,
274|         "dry": dry,
275|         "live": live and not dry,
276|         "planner": planner,
277|         "ok": False,
278|     }
279| 
280|     plan_text = fixture_plan
281|     planner_usage = {"prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0}
282|     planner_error: str | None = None
283| 
284|     if plan_text is None and dry:
285|         plan_text = json.dumps(
286|             {
287|                 "schema": SCHEMA,
288|                 "goal": goal,
289|                 "success_criteria": "read brief + count candidates + note",
290|                 "steps": [
291|                     {"op": "read_file", "path": "memory/improve/field_brief.md"},
292|                     {"op": "count_lines", "path": "memory/improve/candidates.jsonl"},
293|                     {
294|                         "op": "write_run_note",
295|                         "note": "dry fixture: local executed work order without DeepSeek",
296|                     },
297|                 ],
298|             }
299|         )
300|     elif plan_text is None and live:
301|         try:
302|             from models.providers import chat_provider
303| 
304|             system, user = _plan_prompt(goal)
305|             resp = chat_provider(
306|                 planner,
307|                 system,
308|                 user,
309|                 tier="T2",
310|                 max_tokens=800,
311|                 temperature=0.1,
312|             )
313|             if not isinstance(resp, dict):
314|                 raise RuntimeError(f"bad provider response type: {type(resp)}")
315|             if resp.get("ok") is False:
316|                 raise RuntimeError(str(resp.get("error") or resp)[:400])
317|             plan_text = str(
318|                 resp.get("text")
319|                 or resp.get("content")
320|                 or resp.get("message")
321|                 or ""
322|             )
323|             if not plan_text and isinstance(resp.get("result"), str):
324|                 plan_text = resp["result"]
325|             # some adapters nest choices
326|             if not plan_text and resp.get("choices"):
327|                 try:
328|                     plan_text = resp["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
329|                 except Exception:
330|                     pass
331|             planner_usage = _usage_tokens(resp)
332|             out["planner_raw_ok"] = True
333|             out["planner_model"] = resp.get("model") or planner
334|         except Exception as exc:
335|             planner_error = str(exc)[:500]
336|             out["planner_raw_ok"] = False
337|             # fallback canned plan so local half still proves
338|             plan_text = json.dumps(
339|                 {
340|                     "schema": SCHEMA,
341|                     "goal": goal,
342|                     "success_criteria": "fallback local after planner error",
343|                     "steps": [
344|                         {"op": "read_file", "path": "memory/improve/field_brief.md"},
345|                         {
346|                             "op": "write_run_note",
347|                             "note": f"planner failed: {planner_error[:200]}",
348|                         },
349|                     ],
350|                     "planner_fallback": True,
351|                 }
352|             )
353| 
354|     try:
355|         order = parse_work_order(plan_text or "")
356|     except Exception as exc:
357|         out["error"] = f"parse: {exc}"
358|         out["planner_error"] = planner_error
359|         out["plan_text_preview"] = (plan_text or "")[:400]
360|         _write_run(out)
361|         return out
362| 
363|     out["work_order"] = order
364|     out["planner_usage"] = planner_usage
365|     out["planner_error"] = planner_error
366| 
367|     exec_res = execute_work_order(order)
368|     out["execution"] = exec_res
369|     out["ok"] = bool(exec_res.get("ok")) and not planner_error
370| 
371|     # Token thesis: planner should stay small; local exec uses 0 frontier tokens
372|     out["token_thesis"] = {
373|         "frontier_tokens": planner_usage.get("total_tokens") or 0,
374|         "local_llm_tokens": 0,
375|         "local_exec_steps": len(exec_res.get("results") or []),
376|         "claim": (
377|             "DeepSeek plans only (short completion); deterministic local executor "
378|             "does file scut — 0 frontier tool-loop tokens."
379|         ),
380|     }
381|     out["observe"] = {
382|         "run_dir": _rel_posix(RUN_DIR),
383|         "cli": "python main.py token-chain --goal \"...\"",
384|         "dashboard": "POST /api/v1/token-chain",
385|         "latest": "memory/runs/token_chain/latest.json",
386|     }
387|     _write_run(out)
388|     return out
389|

391| def _write_run(out: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
392|     _ensure()
393|     stamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
394|     path = RUN_DIR / f"run-{stamp}.json"
395|     path.write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
396|     (RUN_DIR / "latest.json").write_text(
397|         json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
398|     )
399|     out["artifact"] = _rel_posix(path)
400|

402| def cmd_token_chain(args: Any) -> int:
403|     goal = " ".join(getattr(args, "goal", None) or []) or None
404|     if getattr(args, "goal_text", None):
405|         goal = str(args.goal_text)
406|     res = run_token_chain(
407|         goal=goal,

409|         live=not bool(getattr(args, "dry", False)),

411|     )
412|     print(json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))

1| """tool_manifest — FULL ACCESS to every tool the ghost system exposes, self-updating.
2| 
3| Operator (2026-08-10): "i want to have full access to your tools and understanding of them
4| i want them to all populate directly in vs code". The schema_registry MANIFEST is hand-maintained
5| and only lists ~10 modules; this module AUTO-DISCOVERS every mag/*.py (and tools/*.py) module and
6| extracts, from each module's OWN source (no hand-typing):
7|     SCHEMA            the self-describing version constant
8|     purpose           the first docstring line (or __doc__ head)
9|     CLI               whether it has argparse + its `python -m mag.X ...` line
10|     REST              which /api/v1/... routes it contributes (from dashboard REST if declared)
11|     state_file        where it writes state (heuristic: ROOT / "memory" globs)
12| 
13| It emits a single source-of-truth artifact:
14|     memory/tool_manifest.json   machine-readable (served to the dashboard / REST / VS Code)
15|     TOOLS.md                    human-readable, written to the workspace root (populates in VS Code)
16| 
17| The manifest is the DISCOVERY surface: ghost, the dashboard, and the operator all read the SAME
18| file. Nothing is handwaved — every row is read from the module's own code.
19| 
20| Schema: tool_manifest.v1 · deterministic · $0 (pure AST/token scan, no LLM)
21| CLI:    python -m mag.tool_manifest scan | json | md | status
22| """
23| from __future__ import annotations
24| 
25| import argparse
26| import ast
27| import json
28| import re
29| import sys
30| from datetime import datetime, timezone
31| from pathlib import Path
32| from typing import Any
33| 
34| try:
35|     from config import ROOT
36| except Exception:
37|     ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
38| 
39| sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
40| try:
41|     sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
42| except Exception:
43|     pass
44| 
45| SCHEMA = "tool_manifest.v1"
46| MAG_DIR = ROOT / "mag"
47| TOOLS_DIR = ROOT / "tools"
48| JSON_OUT = ROOT / "memory" / "tool_manifest.json"
49| MD_OUT = ROOT / "TOOLS.md"
50| 
51| # Directory globs the module reads state from — used to guess state_file per module.
52| STATE_HINTS = ["memory", "logs", "state", "configs", "deploy"]
53|

55| def _now() -> str:
56|     return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
57| 
58| 
59| def _head_doc(module_doc: str | None, n: int = 200) -> str:
60|     """First meaningful line of a module docstring -> the 'purpose'.""" 
61|     if not module_doc:
62|         return ""
63|     lines = [ln.strip() for ln in module_doc.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
64|     return (lines[0] if lines else "")[:n]
65| 
66| 
67| def _scan_module(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
68|     """AST-scan ONE module for its self-describing surface (no import, no side effects)."""
69|     name = path.stem
70|     try:
71|         src = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
72|     except OSError:
73|         return {"name": name, "module": f"mag.{name}", "schema": "", "purpose": "UNREADABLE", "ok": False}
74|     try:
75|         tree = ast.parse(src)
76|     except SyntaxError:
77|         return {"name": name, "module": f"mag.{name}", "schema": "", "purpose": "SYNTAX-ERR", "ok": False}
78| 
79|     module_doc = ast.get_docstring(tree) or ""
80|     schema = ""
81|     has_argparse = False
82|     has_http = False
83|     routes: list[str] = []
84|     for node in tree.body:
85|         # SCHEMA = "..."
86|         if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
87|             for t in node.targets:
88|                 if isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == "SCHEMA" and isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant):
89|                     schema = str(node.value.value or "")
90|         # argparse usage (CLI)
91|         if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
92|             for a in node.names:
93|                 if a.name == "argparse":
94|                     has_argparse = True
95|         if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
96|             for a in node.names:
97|                 if a.name == "argparse":
98|                     has_argparse = True
99|         if isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant):
100|             pass
101|     # REST routes: scan the whole source for /api/v1/... path strings
102|     routes = sorted(set(re.findall(r'"/api/v1/[^"]+"', src)))
103|     has_http = bool(routes) or ("http.server" in src or "BaseHTTPRequestHandler" in src)
104| 
105|     cli = ""
106|     if has_argparse or ("if __name__ == '__main__'" in src and "__main__" in src):
107|         cli = f"python -m mag.{name}" if path.parent == MAG_DIR else f"python -m tools.{name}"
108| 
109|     # state_file guess: look for ROOT / "memory" writes declared near the top
110|     state_file = ""
111|     m = re.search(r'([A-Z_]+)\s*=\s*(ROOT|Path\(__file__\)[^)]*)\s*/\s*"((?:memory|logs|state|configs)/[^"]+)"', src)
112|     if m:
113|         state_file = m.group(3)
114| 
115|     return {
116|         "name": name,
117|         "module": f"mag.{name}" if path.parent == MAG_DIR else f"tools.{name}",
118|         "schema": schema or "?",
119|         "purpose": _head_doc(module_doc),
120|         "cli": cli,
121|         "has_http": has_http,
122|         "routes": routes,
123|         "state_file": state_file,
124|         "file": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"),
125|         "ok": True,
126|     }
127| 
128| 
129| def scan() -> dict[str, Any]:
130|     """Discover every mag/*.py + tools/*.py module into the tool manifest."""
131|     mods: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
132|     seen: set[str] = set()
133|     for base, prefix in ((MAG_DIR, "mag"), (TOOLS_DIR, "tools")):
134|         if not base.is_dir():
135|             continue
136|         for p in sorted(base.glob("*.py")):
137|             if p.name.startswith("_"):
138|                 continue
139|             if p.stem in seen:
140|                 continue
141|             seen.add(p.stem)
142|             row = _scan_module(p)
143|             row["module"] = f"{prefix}.{p.stem}"
144|             mods.append(row)
145|     mods.sort(key=lambda m: m["name"])
146|     manifest = {
147|         "schema": SCHEMA,
148|         "ts": _now(),
149|         "n_tools": len(mods),
150|         "tools": mods,
151|     }
152|     JSON_OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
153|     JSON_OUT.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
154|     return manifest
155|

171| def calibrate(*, hours: int = 24, goals: list[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
172|     """Project a goal set and compare to actual provider_usage to learn projection bias.
173| 
174|     Statistical/aggregate (per-model), since per-ask goal linkage needs the session_id we
175|     now capture — this is the honest calibration surface. Returns a per-model correction
176|     factor (projected_input / actual_prompt) to apply to future forecasts.
177|     """

179|     proj = forecast(goal_src)
180|     cutoff = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=hours)).isoformat()
181|     actual: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(lambda: [0.0, 0.0])  # model -> [prompt_tokens, out]
182|     if USAGE.is_file():

184|             if not line.strip():
185|                 continue

188|             except Exception:
189|                 continue
190|             if str(r.get("ts") or "") < cutoff:
191|                 continue
192|             if str(r.get("provider") or "") in ("ollama", "test_provider"):
193|                 continue
194|             m = str(r.get("model") or "?")
195|             actual[m][0] += int(r.get("prompt_tokens") or 0)
196|             actual[m][1] += int(r.get("completion_tokens") or 0)
197|     factors = []

200|         if not a or a[0] <= 0:

202|         ratio = pm["input_tokens_est"] / a[0]
203|         factors.append({"model": pm["model"], "projected_input": pm["input_tokens_est"],
204|                         "actual_prompt": int(a[0]), "correction_factor": round(ratio, 4)})

207|         "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
208|         "window_hours": hours,

151|     """Cross-process single-writer lock for the verkle chain/knots/pointers."""

153|     fd = None
154|     while True:
155|         try:
156|             fd = os.open(str(LOCK), os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)

158|         except FileExistsError:

161|                 # A crashed writer can leave a fresh-looking marker behind (for
162|                 # example after a test/process is terminated).  Do not wait the
163|                 # full 15-minute safety window when the recorded owner is gone.
164|                 if not stale:
165|                     try:
166|                         owner = int(LOCK.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").split()[0])
167|                     except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError):
168|                         owner = 0

173|                             stale = True
174|                         except PermissionError:

176|                             stale = False
177|                         except SystemError:

180|                             stale = True

222| def _merkle_prefix_roots(leaf_hashes: list[str]) -> list[str]:
223|     """Return the legacy duplicate-last Merkle root for every non-empty prefix.
224| 
225|     ``_merkle_root`` duplicates the final node at *each level* when a layer has
226|     odd cardinality. Recomputing that tree for every prefix made an amend
227|     quadratic in the number of leaves. A binary forest stores complete
228|     subtrees as leaves arrive; folding those subtrees right-to-left, lifting a
229|     shorter suffix by self-duplication where necessary, reproduces the legacy
230|     semantics in O(log n) work per prefix. The result is byte-for-byte
231|     equivalent to ``_merkle_root`` for every prefix, but costs O(n log n)
232|     hashes instead of O(n²).
233|     """
234|     if not leaf_hashes:
235|         return []
236| 
237|     def _join(left: str, right: str) -> str:
238|         return _h(b"node:" + left.encode() + b":" + right.encode())
239| 
240|     def _lift(root: str, from_height: int, to_height: int) -> str:
241|         """Apply the same-node duplication until a suffix reaches a height."""
242|         for _ in range(max(0, to_height - from_height)):
243|             root = _join(root, root)
244|         return root
245| 
246|     # (root, height), in left-to-right binary decomposition order. Heights
247|     # descend strictly from left to right, so a right fold is well-defined.
248|     forest: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
249| 
250|     roots: list[str] = []
251|     for leaf in leaf_hashes:
252|         forest.append((leaf, 0))
253|         while len(forest) >= 2 and forest[-1][1] == forest[-2][1]:
254|             right, height = forest.pop()
255|             left, _ = forest.pop()
256|             forest.append((_join(left, right), height + 1))
257| 
258|         root, height = forest[-1]
259|         for left, left_height in reversed(forest[:-1]):
260|             root = _lift(root, height, left_height)
261|             root = _join(left, root)
262|             height = left_height + 1
263|         roots.append(root)
264|     return roots

117| def extract_target(canon: Path = CANON_CARD) -> str:
118|     """Canon card PLAY opening paragraph, markup stripped, text verbatim."""
119|     text = canon.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
120|     i = text.find("## PLAY")
121|     j = text.find("**First chamber", i)
122|     if i < 0 or j < 0:
123|         raise RuntimeError("canon card markers not found (## PLAY / **First chamber)")
124|     body = text[text.find("\n", i) + 1:j]   # skip the rest of the PLAY header line
125|     lines = []
126|     for ln in body.splitlines():
127|         s = ln.strip()
128|         if not s or set(s) == {"-"}:          # dividers
129|             continue
130|         if s.startswith("> "):
131|             s = s[2:]
132|         if s.startswith("- "):
133|             s = s[2:]
134|         lines.append(s.replace("**", "").replace("*", ""))
135|     para = " ".join(" ".join(lines).split())
136|     if len(para) < 200:
137|         raise RuntimeError("target extraction suspiciously short")
138|     return para

215| # ---------------------------------------------------------------- metrics

217| def aligned_span(gen_text: str, tokens: list[str], target: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
218|     """(target-aligned token count, matched char count, offset of the target in
219|     the generation). Harness v2: if the model echoes instruction markers before
220|     the passage (COLD arm did in pass 1), the offset skips them so BOTH arms are
221|     measured over the same target-aligned window; a straddling token at the
222|     offset is skipped (conservative)."""
223|     t = target.strip()
224|     g = gen_text.strip()
225|     anchor = t[:40]
226|     off = g.find(anchor)
227|     if off < 0:
228|         return 0, 0, -1
229|     common = 0
230|     for a, b in zip(g[off:], t):
231|         if a != b:
232|             break
233|         common += 1
234|     matched, acc, started = 0, 0, False
235|     for tok in tokens:
236|         if not started:
237|             if acc + len(tok) <= off:
238|                 acc += len(tok)
239|                 continue
240|             started = True     # token straddles the offset — skip it
241|             acc += len(tok)
242|             continue
243|         if acc + len(tok) <= off + common:
244|             acc += len(tok)
245|             matched += 1
246|         else:
247|             break
248|     return matched, common, off

251| def metrics(resp: dict[str, Any], target: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
252|     lps = resp.get("logprobs") or []
253|     tokens = [str(e.get("token", "")) for e in lps]
254|     sel = [float(e.get("logprob", 0.0)) for e in lps]
255|     gen = str((resp.get("message") or {}).get("content", ""))
256|     # integrity on this host (v0.32.7): eval_count = len(logprobs)+1, but the lp
257|     # token concat covers the FULL generated content — that is the real gate.
258|     concat_ok = "".join(tokens) == gen
259|     span, common_chars, off = aligned_span(gen, tokens, target)
260|     exact = gen.strip() == target.strip()
261|     contained = target.strip() in gen.strip()
262|     low_align = span < MIN_ALIGNED
263|     n = span
264|     i0 = _token_index_at_offset(tokens, off) if off > 0 else 0
265|     seg = sel[i0:i0 + n]
266|     mean_lp = sum(seg) / len(seg) if seg else float("nan")
267|     ppl = math.exp(mean_lp) if seg else float("nan")
268|     full_mean = sum(sel) / len(sel) if sel else float("nan")
269|     return {
270|         "n_generated": len(sel),
271|         "eval_count": resp.get("eval_count"),
272|         "lp_covers_content": concat_ok,
273|         "exact_copy": exact,
274|         "target_contained": contained,
275|         "aligned_tokens": span,
276|         "matched_chars": common_chars,
277|         "target_offset_in_gen": off,
278|         "low_align": low_align,
279|         "primary_span": len(seg),
280|         "mean_logprob": round(mean_lp, 6),
281|         "ppl": round(ppl, 6),
282|         "mean_logprob_full": round(full_mean, 6),
283|         "ppl_full": round(math.exp(full_mean), 6) if sel else float("nan"),
284|         "gen_sha16": _sha16(gen),
285|         "gen_head": gen[:96],
286|         "selected_logprobs": [round(x, 6) for x in seg],
287|         "timing": {
288|             "prompt_eval_count": resp.get("prompt_eval_count"),
289|             "prompt_eval_ms": round((resp.get("prompt_eval_duration") or 0) / 1e6, 1),
290|             "eval_count": resp.get("eval_count"),
291|             "eval_ms": round((resp.get("eval_duration") or 0) / 1e6, 1),
292|             "total_ms": round((resp.get("total_duration") or 0) / 1e6, 1),
293|         },
294|     }

297| def _token_index_at_offset(tokens: list[str], off: int) -> int:
298|     """Index of the first token fully at/after char offset `off`."""
299|     acc = 0
300|     for i, tok in enumerate(tokens):
301|         if acc >= off:
302|             return i
303|         acc += len(tok)
304|     return len(tokens)

310|         return round(t["prompt_eval_ms"] / t["prompt_eval_count"], 3)
311|     return None

316| def run(rounds: int = ROUNDS, model: str = PRIMARY_MODEL) -> int:

323|           f"(genome 3000c + {TAKE_ROWS} tape rows, labeled)")

326|     rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

328|     def emit(row: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
329|         row.update({
330|             "schema": "warmed_cold_replay.v1",

332|             "instrument": "mag/warmed_cold_replay.py",
333|             "specimen": model,
334|             "label": LABEL,

337|             "thresholds": THRESHOLDS,

344|     # warmup: load weights only (a 1-token call; NOT a metric)

347|          num_predict=1)
348|     print(f"warmup (weights loaded): {time.perf_counter() - t0:.1f}s")
349| 
350|     arms = {
351|         "RESURRECTED": [{"role": "system", "content": c["preload"]},
352|                         {"role": "user", "content": c["user"]}],
353|         "COLD": [{"role": "user", "content": c["user"]}],
354|     }
355| 
356|     measured: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {a: [] for a in arms}
357|     for rnd in range(1, rounds + 1):
358|         for arm in ("RESURRECTED", "COLD"):
359|             t0 = time.perf_counter()
360|             resp = chat(arms[arm], logprobs=True, model=model)
361|             m = metrics(resp, c["target"])
362|             m["prefill_ms_per_tok"] = prefill_ms_per_tok(m)
363|             measured[arm].append(m)
364|             emit({"kind": "call", "arm": arm, "round": rnd, "mode": "logprobs",
365|                   "wall_s": round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 1), **m})
366|             print(f"[{arm} r{rnd}] ppl={m['ppl']:.4f} mean_lp={m['mean_logprob']:.4f} "
367|                   f"exact={m['exact_copy']} contained={m['target_contained']} "
368|                   f"aligned={m['aligned_tokens']} off={m['target_offset_in_gen']} "
369|                   f"lp_cover={m['lp_covers_content']} "
370|                   f"prefill={m['timing']['prompt_eval_ms']}ms/"
371|                   f"{m['timing']['prompt_eval_count']}tok")
372| 
373|     # observer-effect guard: one logprobs-free run per arm
374|     observer: dict[str, bool] = {}
375|     for arm in ("RESURRECTED", "COLD"):

377|         gen = str((resp.get("message") or {}).get("content", ""))
378|         same = _sha16(gen) == measured[arm][0]["gen_sha16"]

380|         emit({"kind": "guard", "arm": arm, "mode": "no_logprobs",

384|     # aggregates — only target-aligned rounds enter the primary metric
385|     def agg(arm: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
386|         all_ms = measured[arm]
387|         ms = [m for m in all_ms if m["aligned_tokens"] > 0]
388|         ppls = [m["ppl"] for m in ms]
389|         lps = [m["mean_logprob"] for m in ms]

391|         spread = (max(ppls) - min(ppls)) / mean_ppl if mean_ppl else float("nan")
392|         return {"ppl_mean": round(mean_ppl, 6), "ppl_min": round(min(ppls), 6),
393|                 "ppl_max": round(max(ppls), 6), "stability_spread": round(spread, 6),
394|                 "mean_lp_mean": round(sum(lps) / len(lps), 6),
395|                 "aligned_rounds": len(ms),
396|                 "excluded_rounds_unaligned": len(all_ms) - len(ms),
397|                 "exact_rounds": sum(1 for m in ms if m["exact_copy"]),
398|                 "contained_rounds": sum(1 for m in ms if m["target_contained"]),
399|                 "lp_cover_rounds": sum(1 for m in ms if m["lp_covers_content"])}
400| 
401|     a_res, a_cold = agg("RESURRECTED"), agg("COLD")
402|     ppl_d = (a_cold["ppl_mean"] - a_res["ppl_mean"]) / a_cold["ppl_mean"] * 100
403|     lp_d = a_res["mean_lp_mean"] - a_cold["mean_lp_mean"]
404|     if ppl_d < THRESHOLDS["not_real"]:
405|         verdict = "RESURRECTION-NOT-REAL (preload is decoration at this scale)"
406|     elif ppl_d <= THRESHOLDS["measured"]:

408|     else:
409|         verdict = "LARGE_EFFECT (preload dominates at PROXY scale; production claims stay with witness #3)"
410| 
411|     # timing leg (W3): classify EVERY round warm/cold by an absolute threshold —
412|     # on this host genuine cold prefill runs 2.3-5.9 ms/tok, KV hits < 0.1 ms/tok
413|     # (observed). Round 1 can still be a HIT (identical prompt served <20 min ago
414|     # under keep_alive), so coldness is measured, never assumed.
415|     def timing_leg(arm: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
416|         ms = measured[arm]
417|         rounds = []
418|         colds, warms = [], []
419|         for i, m in enumerate(ms):
420|             pt = m["prefill_ms_per_tok"]
421|             hit = pt is not None and pt < 0.5
422|             rounds.append({"round": i + 1, "prefill_ms_per_tok": pt,
423|                            "cache": "warm" if hit else "cold"})
424|             (warms if hit else colds).append(pt or 0.0)
425|         cold = round(sum(colds) / len(colds), 3) if colds else None
426|         warm = round(sum(warms) / len(warms), 4) if warms else None
427|         return {"cold_prefill_ms_per_tok": cold,
428|                 "warm_prefill_ms_per_tok": warm,
429|                 "warm_speedup_x": round(cold / warm, 1) if cold and warm else None,
430|                 "n_cold_rounds": len(colds), "n_warm_rounds": len(warms),
431|                 "rounds": rounds}
432| 
433|     summary = {
434|         "kind": "summary",
435|         "ppl_resurrected_mean": a_res["ppl_mean"],
436|         "ppl_cold_mean": a_cold["ppl_mean"],
437|         "ppl_delta_pct": round(ppl_d, 2),
438|         "mean_lp_resurrected": a_res["mean_lp_mean"],
439|         "mean_lp_cold": a_cold["mean_lp_mean"],
440|         "mean_lp_delta_nats": round(lp_d, 6),
441|         "stability": {"RESURRECTED": a_res, "COLD": a_cold},
442|         "exact_copy_rounds": {"RESURRECTED": a_res["exact_rounds"],
443|                               "COLD": a_cold["exact_rounds"]},
444|         "target_contained_rounds": {"RESURRECTED": a_res["contained_rounds"],
445|                                     "COLD": a_cold["contained_rounds"]},
446|         "timing_leg_W3": {"RESURRECTED": timing_leg("RESURRECTED"),
447|                           "COLD": timing_leg("COLD")},
448|         "observer_effect_ok": observer,
449|         "verdict": verdict,
450|         "honesty": "PROXY (3B carrier): instrument's question only - production "
451|                    "resurrection fidelity stays with Astra witness #3",
452|     }
453|     emit(summary)
454| 
455|     print("\n==== WARMED-VS-COLD REPLAY SUMMARY ====")
456|     print(f"ppl resurrected={a_res['ppl_mean']}  cold={a_cold['ppl_mean']}")
457|     print(f"ppl delta = {ppl_d:.2f}%   mean lp delta = {lp_d:+.4f} nats")
458|     print(f"stability spread: res={a_res['stability_spread']} cold={a_cold['stability_spread']}")
459|     print(f"timing leg (W3): res={summary['timing_leg_W3']['RESURRECTED']} "
460|           f"cold={summary['timing_leg_W3']['COLD']}")
461|     print(f"observer effect ok: {observer}")
462|     print(f"VERDICT: {verdict}")
463|     print(f"rows: {OUT_ROWS}")
464|     return 0

33| # Warning-ish line patterns. Deliberately broad; the signature-dedup + length

51|         return set()
52|     try:
53|         data = json.loads(seen_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
54|         return set(data.get("seen", []) or [])
55|     except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):

59| def _save_seen(seen: set[str], seen_path: Path) -> None:

63| 
64| def _normalize(line: str) -> str:
65|     return " ".join(line.split()).strip()

72| def extract_warnings(*, log_dir: Path = LOG_DIR, tail: int = 400) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
73|     """Scan textual process logs and pull warning/error lines.

77|     out: list[dict[str, str]] = []
78|     seen_sig: set[str] = set()

80|         return out

87|             text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

89|         except OSError:

98|             if sig in seen_sig:

53| def fire_lane(lane: dict, pack: str, live: set, outdir: pathlib.Path) -> dict:

65|                "max_tokens": lane.get("max_tokens", 8192), "temperature": lane.get("temperature", 0.4)}

84|     except Exception as e:
85|         rec.update({"status": "fail", "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:140]}"})
86|     (outdir / f"{lane_id}.receipt.json").write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

90| def run(pack_path: str, lanes_path: str, outdir: str, workers: int = 12) -> int:

92|     lanes = json.loads(pathlib.Path(lanes_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

98|     key_env = lanes[0]["key_env"]
99|     url = lanes[0]["url"]
100|     key = os.environ.get(key_env, "")
101|     slugs = sorted({l["model"] for l in lanes} | set(probe_route.FALLBACK_CHAIN))
102|     rows = [probe_route.probe_one(s, url, key) for s in slugs]
103|     live = {r["slug"] for r in rows if r["verdict"] in {"live", "flaky"}}
104|     breaker_state = lane_breaker._load().get("suspended", {})
105|     suspended = {f"wave:{s}" for s in list(live) if f"wave:{s}" in breaker_state}
106|     live -= suspended
107|     gate = {"slugs_probed": len(rows), "live": sorted(live), "suspended_refused": sorted(suspended),
108|             "excluded": [{"slug": r["slug"], "verdict": r["verdict"]} for r in rows if r["verdict"] == "dead"]}
109|     (out / "GATE.json").write_text(json.dumps(gate, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
110|     print(f"GATE: {len(live)} live, {len(gate['excluded'])} dead, {len(suspended)} suspended-refused", flush=True)
111| 
112|     # 2. FIRE
113|     with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
114|         receipts = list(pool.map(lambda l: fire_lane(l, pack, live, out), lanes))
115|     for r in receipts:
116|         print(f"{r['lane']} [{r.get('routed_slug')}]: {r['status']} {r.get('completion_tokens','')}tok", flush=True)
117| 
118|     # 3+4. MEASURE + BREAK — per-slug success ratio into the breaker (only on >=2-lane
119|     # samples; a perfect wave auto-clears its suspension so one bad wave can't brick the pool)
120|     by_slug = {}
121|     for r in receipts:
122|         by_slug.setdefault(r.get("routed_slug"), []).append(1 if r["status"] == "ok" else 0)
123|     verdicts = {}
124|     for slug, oks in by_slug.items():
125|         ratio = sum(oks) / len(oks)
126|         if ratio == 1.0:
127|             lane_breaker.clear(f"wave:{slug}", note="perfect wave — auto-clear")
128|             verdicts[slug] = {"ratio": ratio, "action": "clear"}
129|         elif len(oks) >= 2:

131|         else:
132|             verdicts[slug] = {"ratio": ratio, "action": "unsampled(<2), not tripped"}

134|                                                "breaker": verdicts, "wall_s": round(time.time() - t0, 1)},
135|                                               indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
136|     tripped = [s for s, v in verdicts.items() if v.get("tripped")]
137|     print(f"WAVE DONE {time.time()-t0:.1f}s — breaker tripped: {tripped or 'none'}", flush=True)
138|     return 0
139| 
140| 
141| def main() -> int:
142|     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wave_fire")
143|     ap.add_argument("action", choices=["run"])
144|     ap.add_argument("--pack", required=True)
145|     ap.add_argument("--lanes", required=True)
146|     ap.add_argument("--outdir", required=True)
147|     ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=12)
148|     a = ap.parse_args()

272| def is_strike_chord_prompt(text: str) -> bool:
273|     """Heuristic: does this post look like a Strike the Chord AI system prompt?
274| 
275|     Checks for:
276|     - Contains multiple strike patterns (system prompt structure)
277|     - Minimum length (real prompts are long)
278|     - Contains function/tool definitions
279|     - Contains behavioral guidelines
280|     """
281|     if len(text) < STRIKE_MIN_LENGTH:
282|         return False
283| 
284|     matches = 0
285|     for pattern in STRIKE_PATTERNS:
286|         if re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
287|             matches += 1
288| 
289|     # Need at least 3 pattern matches for high confidence
290|     return matches >= 3

293| def extract_prompt_metadata(text: str, post_id: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
294|     """Extract metadata from a Strike the Chord prompt.
295| 
296|     Detects: model name, date/version, tool list, team structure.
297|     """
298|     meta: dict[str, Any] = {
299|         "post_id": post_id,
300|         "is_strike_chord": False,
301|         "detected_model": "",
302|         "detected_date": "",
303|         "tool_count": 0,
304|         "team_agents": [],
305|         "has_tools": False,
306|         "has_render_components": False,
307|         "char_length": len(text),
308|     }
309| 
310|     if not is_strike_chord_prompt(text):
311|         return meta
312| 
313|     meta["is_strike_chord"] = True
314| 
315|     # Detect model name
316|     model_patterns = [
317|         r"(?:you are|as)\s+(Grok[\s\-]?[\d\.]+(?:\s*\([^)]+\))?)",
318|         r"(?:you are|as)\s+(Claude[\s\-]?[\d\.]+(?:\s*\([^)]+\))?)",
319|         r"(?:you are|as)\s+(GPT[\s\-]?[\d\.]+(?:\s*\([^)]+\))?)",
320|         r"(?:you are|as)\s+(Gemini[\s\-]?[\d\.]+(?:\s*\([^)]+\))?)",
321|     ]
322|     for pat in model_patterns:
323|         m = re.search(pat, text, re.IGNORECASE)
324|         if m:
325|             meta["detected_model"] = m.group(1).strip()
326|             break
327| 
328|     # Detect date
329|     date_patterns = [
330|         r'(?:updated|version|release)[:\s]+([A-Z][a-z]{2}[-\s]\d{1,2}[,\s]*2025)',
331|         r'(?:updated|version|release)[:\s]+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})',
332|     ]
333|     for pat in date_patterns:
334|         m = re.search(pat, text, re.IGNORECASE)
335|         if m:
336|             meta["detected_date"] = m.group(1).strip()
337|             break
338| 
339|     # Count tools
340|     tool_matches = re.findall(r'\{"name":\s*"(\w+)",\s*"description"', text)
341|     meta["tool_count"] = len(tool_matches)
342|     meta["has_tools"] = meta["tool_count"] > 0
343| 
344|     # Detect render components
345|     meta["has_render_components"] = bool(re.search(r'Render\s+Components', text, re.I))
346| 
347|     # Detect team agents
348|     team_match = re.search(
349|         r'(?:collaborating with|team[:\s]+)([^.!?\n]{10,100})',
350|         text, re.IGNORECASE,
351|     )
352|     if team_match:
353|         names = re.findall(r'\b([A-Z][a-z]+)\b', team_match.group(1))
354|         meta["team_agents"] = names[:6]
355| 
356|     return meta
357|

95| def _b64url(b: bytes) -> str:

103| # ── PKCE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
104| def _make_pkce() -> tuple[str, str]:
105|     verifier = _b64url(secrets.token_bytes(48))
106|     challenge = _b64url(hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode("ascii")).digest())
107|     return verifier, challenge

110| # ── Step 1: build authorize URL ─────────────────────────────────────
111| def start(*, auto_server: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
112|     if not _configured():
113|         return {"ok": False, "schema": SCHEMA,
114|                 "error": "X_CLIENT_ID not set — create an X developer app and fill .env"}
115|     verifier, challenge = _make_pkce()
116|     state = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
117|     _write_json(OAUTH_STATE, {"verifier": verifier, "state": state, "ts": _now()})
118|     params = {
119|         "response_type": "code",
120|         "client_id": CLIENT_ID,
121|         "redirect_uri": REDIRECT_URI,
122|         "scope": SCOPES,
123|         "state": state,
124|         "code_challenge": challenge,
125|         "code_challenge_method": "S256",
126|     }
127|     url = f"{AUTHORIZE_URL}?{urlencode(params)}"
128|     if auto_server:
129|         threading.Thread(target=_run_callback_server, daemon=True).start()
130|     webbrowser.open(url)

132|             "redirect_uri": REDIRECT_URI,
133|             "note": "open the URL, log in as the account, authorize. Code auto-captured."}

139| def _run_callback_server() -> None:
140|     class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
141|         def do_GET(self):
142|             q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
143|             _captured["code"] = q.get("code", [""])[0]
144|             _captured["state"] = q.get("state", [""])[0]
145|             body = b"Authorization captured. You can close this tab and return to the terminal."
146|             self.send_response(200)
147|             self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
148|             self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
149|             self.end_headers()
150|             self.wfile.write(body)

152|         def log_message(self, *a):
153|             pass

155|     port = int(urlparse(REDIRECT_URI).port or 8788)
156|     try:
157|         HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), H).handle_request()
158|     except OSError:
159|         pass

164|     st = _read_json(OAUTH_STATE)

168|     data = {
169|         "code": code,
170|         "grant_type": "authorization_code",
171|         "client_id": CLIENT_ID,
172|         "redirect_uri": REDIRECT_URI,
173|         "code_verifier": verifier,
174|     }
175|     if CLIENT_SECRET:
176|         data["client_secret"] = CLIENT_SECRET

178|         r = requests.post(TOKEN_URL, data=data, timeout=30)
179|     except requests.RequestException as e:

183|     tok = r.json()

186|         "refresh_token": tok.get("refresh_token", ""),

188|         "scope": tok.get("scope", ""),

248| def upload_media(image_path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
249|     """v2 simple media upload (images <=5MB). Returns {media_id}."""
250|     at, err = _access_token()

253|     p = Path(image_path)

258|         return {"ok": False, "schema": SCHEMA, "error": f"file too large: {len(raw)} B"}
259|     mime = "image/png" if raw[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" else (
260|         "image/jpeg" if raw[:3] == b"\xff\xd8\xff" else "application/octet-stream")
261|     if mime == "application/octet-stream":
262|         return {"ok": False, "schema": SCHEMA, "error": "not a PNG/JPEG"}

266|             headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {at}", "User-Agent": f"{HANDLE}/0.1"},
267|             files={"media": (p.name, raw, mime)},

467| def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
468|     import argparse
469|     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="x-oauth")
470|     ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=["start", "complete", "post", "me", "refresh", "like", "follow", "recent", "dm", "edit", "delete", "status"])
471|     ap.add_argument("arg", nargs="*", default=[])
472|     args, _unknown = ap.parse_known_args(argv)
473|     args.arg = (args.arg or []) + _unknown
474|     body = " ".join(args.arg)
475|     if args.cmd == "start":
476|         print(json.dumps(start(), indent=2))
477|         # wait briefly for the callback server to capture a code
478|         for _ in range(120):
479|             if _captured.get("code"):
480|                 break
481|             import time
482|             time.sleep(0.5)
483|         if _captured.get("code"):
484|             print(json.dumps(complete(_captured["code"]), indent=2))
485|     elif args.cmd == "complete":
486|         print(json.dumps(complete(body), indent=2))
487|     elif args.cmd == "post":
488|         # post "<text>" | post --media <path> --reply <tweet_id> "<text>"
489|         # flags are stripped from ANYWHERE in the arg list (order-free)
490|         mid, rto = "", ""
491|         rest, flags = [], {}
492|         pending = None
493|         for a in args.arg:
494|             if a in ("--media", "--reply"):
495|                 pending = a
496|             elif pending == "--media":
497|                 flags["media"] = a; pending = None
498|             elif pending == "--reply":
499|                 flags["reply"] = a; pending = None
500|             else:
501|                 rest.append(a)
502|         if "media" in flags:
503|             up = upload_media(flags["media"])
504|             if not up.get("ok"):
505|                 print(json.dumps(up, indent=2)); sys.exit(1)
506|             mid = up.get("media_id", "")
507|         rto = flags.get("reply", "")
508|         body = " ".join(rest)
509|         print(json.dumps(post(body, [mid] if mid else None, rto), indent=2))
510|     elif args.cmd == "edit":
511|         # python -m mag.x_oauth edit "<post_id>" "<text>"
512|         parts = [a for a in args.arg if a.strip()]
513|         if len(parts) < 2:

89| def _copy_canonical_to_derived(src: Path, dst: Path) -> str:
90|     """One-way copy canonical -> derived (site/dist is a build target, never a source).
91| 
92|     Plain copy semantics: derived mtime updates to now (no mtime preservation).
93|     Drift guard: if the derived copy is NEWER than its canonical source AND the
94|     bytes differ, someone edited derived output directly — refuse to overwrite,
95|     name both files, surface it. Identical-newer bytes = lockstep, harmless skip."""
96|     if dst.exists() and dst.stat().st_mtime > src.stat().st_mtime:
97|         if _same_bytes(dst, src):
98|             return "lockstep"
99|         print("WARNING: drift — derived file is NEWER than its canonical source; refusing to overwrite.")
100|         print(f"  derived  (newer, edited directly?): {dst}")
101|         print(f"  canonical (source of truth):         {src}")
102|         print("  reconcile: canonical wins — re-land the work on canonical, then rerun this builder.")
103|         return "refused"
104|     dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
105|     shutil.copy(src, dst)
106|     return "copied"

156| def sample_peaks(pids: list[int], watch_seconds: float, vm_probe=None) -> tuple[int | None, float | None]:
157|     """Peak concurrent memory across --watch-seconds: (peak_rss_bytes_sum, peak_vm_gib)."""
158|     peak_rss: int | None = None
159|     peak_vm: float | None = None
160|     deadline = time.monotonic() + max(watch_seconds, 0.0)
161|     while True:
162|         vals = [rss_bytes(p) for p in pids]
163|         vals = [v for v in vals if v is not None]
164|         if vals:
165|             s = sum(vals)
166|             peak_rss = s if peak_rss is None else max(peak_rss, s)
167|         vm = vm_probe() if vm_probe else None
168|         if vm is not None:
169|             peak_vm = vm if peak_vm is None else max(peak_vm, vm)
170|         if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
171|             break
172|         time.sleep(1.0)
173|     return peak_rss, peak_vm

178| def load_run(telemetry_path: Path, ticklog_dir: Path | None = None):
179|     telem = json.loads(telemetry_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
180|     run_id = telem.get("run_id", "unknown")
181|     lanes = telem.get("lanes", [])
182|     tick_seconds = telem.get("tick_seconds")
183|     ticks = telem.get("of")
184|     # ticklog (same run dir) gives per-tick wall deltas + dock latency
185|     if ticklog_dir is None:
186|         ticklog_dir = ROOT / "memory" / "runs" / "trailer"
187|     ticklog = ticklog_dir / run_id / "ticklog.jsonl"
188|     tick_deltas_ms: list[float] = []
189|     dock_ms: list[float] = []
190|     log_tick_seconds = None
191|     if ticklog.exists():
192|         prev_ts = None
193|         for line in ticklog.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
194|             try:
195|                 row = json.loads(line)
196|             except json.JSONDecodeError:
197|                 continue
198|             if row.get("row") == "header":
199|                 log_tick_seconds = row.get("tick_seconds")
200|                 ticks = ticks or row.get("duration_ticks")
201|                 prev_ts = None
202|                 continue
203|             ts = row.get("ts")
204|             if prev_ts and ts:
205|                 from datetime import datetime as _dt
206|                 d = (_dt.fromisoformat(ts) - _dt.fromisoformat(prev_ts)).total_seconds()
207|                 if 0 < d < 600:
208|                     tick_deltas_ms.append(round(d * 1000.0, 1))
209|             prev_ts = ts
210|             for ln in row.get("lanes", []):
211|                 if ln.get("docked") and isinstance(ln.get("ms"), (int, float)):
212|                     dock_ms.append(float(ln["ms"]))
213|     return {
214|         "run_id": run_id,
215|         "lanes": lanes,
216|         "tick_seconds": log_tick_seconds or tick_seconds,
217|         "ticks": ticks,
218|         "tick_deltas_ms": tick_deltas_ms,
219|         "dock_ms": dock_ms,

223| def measure_rung(rung: str, width: int, label: str, run: dict,

225|     lanes = run["lanes"]

227|     measured = len(lanes) >= width  # full width carried, or the rung is Unproven
228|     sub = lanes[:present] if measured else []
229|     falls = sum(int(l.get("falls", 0)) for l in sub)
230|     docks = sum(int(l.get("accepted", 0)) for l in sub)
231|     hold = sum(int(l.get("hold_seconds", 0)) for l in sub)
232|     tsec = run["tick_seconds"]
233|     denom = {
234|         "lanes": width,
235|         "tick_seconds": tsec,
236|         "ticks": run["ticks"],
237|         "ops": (width * run["ticks"]) if (tsec and run["ticks"]) else None,
238|     }
239|     tripped = vm_gib is not None and vm_gib > KILL_LIMIT_GIB
240|     row = {
241|         "schema": SCHEMA,
242|         "row": "rung",
243|         "ts": now_iso(),
244|         "run_id": run["run_id"],
245|         "rung": rung,
246|         "width": width,
247|         "label": label,
248|         "denominator": denom,
249|         "measured": measured,
250|         "lanes_present": present,
251|         "falls": falls if measured else None,
252|         "docks": docks if measured else None,
253|         "hold_seconds": hold if measured else None,
254|         "falls_per_lane": (round(falls / present, 3) if measured and present else None),
255|         "tick_duration_ms_median": (median(run["tick_deltas_ms"]) if measured and run["tick_deltas_ms"] else None),
256|         "dock_ms_median": (median(run["dock_ms"]) if measured and run["dock_ms"] else None),
257|         "peak_rss_bytes": peak_rss,
258|         "peak_rss_gib": (round(peak_rss / (1024.0 ** 3), 4) if peak_rss else None),
259|         "vm_observed_gib": vm_gib,
260|         "kill": {
261|             "metric": "vm_observed_gib",
262|             "limit_gib": KILL_LIMIT_GIB,
263|             "observed_gib": vm_gib,
264|             "tripped": tripped,
265|         },
266|         "status": ("LOUD" if tripped else ("PASS" if measured else "UNMEASURED")),

257| def preserve_live_desk(paths: tuple[Path, ...] | None = None) -> Callable[[], None]:

271|             else:

273|                 path.write_bytes(content)
274|         restored = True

7| 
8| STAGE 1 (visible battery) — checks the organs were BUILT against:
9|   queue:  todo.md checkbox status counts parse; queue_events.jsonl rows parse
10|           with ts+event; drain task_ids nonempty.
11|   room:   every watch/room.jsonl row parses as JSON; required identity keys

17|           strings ("Legendre", "leaf:", "launched law").
18| 
19| STAGE 2 (held-out battery) — DIFFERENT checks on DIFFERENT slices, per the
20| paper's finding that self-improvement gains fail to generalize to unseen
21| tasks. Nothing here was a build-time invariant:
22|   queue:  deeper slice — queue/handoff/cloud-*.json handoffs: schema field,
23|           parseable ts, unique run_ids, stale (>30d) handoffs flagged.
24|   room:   different date range — rows BEFORE 2026-09-03 (the first half of
25|           the log) re-checked for keys, ts ISO-parseability, and global
26|           timestamp monotonicity.
27|   falsifiers: different surface — markers verified in the FILES ON DISK
28|           (server-independent) plus <title> well-formedness, instead of HTTP.
29| 
30| STAGE 1 score may be near-perfect while STAGE 2 diverges; that divergence is
31| the brittle-generalization signal the paper measures. Measure, never fix.
32| 
33| Usage: .venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/harness_eval.py
34| Output: JSON to stdout; appended to memory/runs/harness_eval/eval_<ts>.json.
35| Zero deps beyond stdlib.
36| """

38| from __future__ import annotations

40| import json
41| import re
42| import sys
43| import time
44| import urllib.request
45| from datetime import datetime, timezone

48| ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
49| QUEUE_EVENTS = ROOT / "logs" / "queue_events.jsonl"
50| QUEUE_TODO = ROOT / "queue" / "todo.md"
51| QUEUE_CLAIMS = ROOT / "logs" / "queue_gate_claims.jsonl"
52| QUEUE_HANDOFF = ROOT / "queue" / "handoff"
53| ROOM = ROOT / "watch" / "room.jsonl"
54| BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8765"
55| STALE_HOURS = 48
56| HANDOFF_STALE_DAYS = 30
57| HELD_OUT_CUTOFF = "2026-09-03"  # stage-2 room slice: strictly before this date

70| def _read_jsonl(path: Path):

172| class Worker:

186|             creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0),

197|         self.proc.stdin.write(nonce.hex().encode() + b"\n")
